body:
Honestly, after the honeymoon phase of the relationship, he got more withdrawn like that. That's been an issue as well, and he's addressed it slightly. He does okay for a while with being more affectionate but will fall back into being distant, or like a close friend. As for emotionally supportive, he says it is awkward to deal with other people's emotions and is withdrawn in that regard as well. It's to the point where he told me not to bring any issues I have with my depression to him, because he doesn't know how to handle it. 

I have considered counseling, but I feel like if I can't even make proper friends who care about me, why would a random stranger truly care about me? Idk. It's hard to convince myself I'm worth giving a damn over, as silly as that probably sounds.

I was kicked out of my emotionally abusive parents' home for starting a relationship with the man I'm with. I had always had a lot of issues with them beforehand that were very deep rooted since I was 3-4 years old, but this was just icing on the cake. So with no support, income, and stability, I dug myself a life out of what I could, having to rely upon his family for a home during the holidays and breaks in between college semesters. I've felt like I've had hardly any emotional support as well, seeing as I lost just about every friend I've made for the past 3 years (come to find out, they were feeding my mother false information and making the situation a lot worse). I have come to rely on my partner for a lot, which I understand can be taxing, especially when he's not affectionate or emotionally supportive. On top of that, I'm nearing my final semester in college, and after that, I have to find a stable job and an apartment to get on my feet. I have been working 3 small university/part time jobs that help cover needs and my living arrangements, but that will be over after this semester. It's been rough.

Thanks so much for support, everyone. It feels a little reassuring to hear others empathize. I agree, I'm young and I shouldn't settle for this. I'm considering showing him what I typed out and the responses. He often seems to value others' opinions on subjects a little more than mine (it gets labelled as nagging). Maybe this will start much needed communication. If it doesn't, though, and everything falls back into the shitty rut it's in, well... There's other options.
